articles.title: India LNG Train Flagged Off as Railways Cut Diesel Use - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News India’s First LNG Train Flagged Off as Railways Push Diesel Cuts Breaking News India’s First LNG Train Flagged Off as Railways Push Diesel Cuts By Urban Acres September 28, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp India’s first LNG-powered train was flagged off from Sabarmati railway station in Gujarat on Sunday, alongside the inauguration and foundation-laying of railway projects valued at more than Rs 1,500 crore. The projects include line doubling, the Kavach train protection system, automatic signalling and a maintenance shed for WAG-12 electric locomotives. Union home minister Amit Shah flagged off the LNG-powered train at an event in Sabarmati and also launched a WAG-12 electric locomotive. The initiatives come as Indian Railways continues to expand electrification, increase network capacity and reduce its dependence on diesel. According to statements reported by the Times News Network, Shah said railway modernisation since 2014 had included the dedicated freight corridor, the rapid rail system and premium railway stations. He also referred to the development of hydrogen-powered train technology, although the event covered the flag-off of an LNG-powered train. The railway works announced in Gujarat combine capacity expansion with operational and safety upgrades. Line doubling is intended to provide additional track capacity on busy routes, while automatic signalling can support train movements across sections where traffic volumes are increasing. The projects also include the Kavach train protection system, which is designed to support railway safety operations, and a dedicated maintenance shed for WAG-12 electric locomotives. Shah said an 11,000-kilometre rail corridor was being converted into a four-track network to improve traffic movement and operational efficiency. The statement did not specify the sections included in this conversion or provide a completion timeline for the entire programme. The LNG train launch also comes against the backdrop of a broader shift in railway fuel use. Shah said Indian Railways consumed 293 crore litres of diesel in 2015-16, compared with 108 crore litres in 2024-25. He said diesel consumption was expected to reach zero by 2030, which would reduce foreign-exchange expenditure. The figures and target were presented at the event and were not accompanied in the report by a separate project-wise implementation plan. Railway electrification has reached 99.6%, according to Shah, with the remaining network expected to be electrified soon. He compared India’s reported electrification level with figures cited for China, Spain, France and the United Kingdom, saying India was on course to achieve full electrification. The shift away from diesel has implications for how Indian Railways plans its traction systems, maintenance facilities and fuel procurement. LNG-powered trains can form part of that transition, but the report does not specify the route, operating frequency, fuel capacity or long-term deployment plan for the train flagged off from Sabarmati. Gujarat’s railway allocation has also increased sharply, Shah said, from Rs 589 crore during 2009-14 to Rs 17,366 crore in 2026-27. articles.title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG-powered train, inaugurates Rs 1472 crore railway ...
articles.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India September 27, 2026 5:57 PM IST Amit Shah | Indian railways | Ministry of Railways | Ahmedabad | railway projects | LNG powered train Amit Shah flags off India’s first LNG-powered train, inaugurates Rs 1,472 crore railway projects in Ahmedabad Author: DD India Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday inaugurated development projects worth ₹1,472 crore and flagged off the country’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. HM Shah also inaugurated a WAG-12 Maintenance Shed, constructed at a cost of ₹700 crore for maintenance of railway locomotive engines. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and other dignitaries were present at the programme. HM Shah said the LNG-powered train would contribute to environmental protection and described the various railway projects as significant for environmental sustainability, passenger amenities and railway safety. He said the Sabarmati railway area had undergone substantial transformation in passenger amenities, safety and connectivity. Recalling Sabarmati’s association with Mahatma Gandhi’s experiments with Satyagraha, simple living, rural development and khadi, HM Shah said the journey of translating these ideas into action had begun from Sabarmati. ₹1,472 crore projects and Kavach safety system The projects inaugurated and launched during the programme include the WAG-12 Maintenance Shed, installation of the Kavach train protection system on the Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati section and the commencement of Kavach-related work on the Ahmedabad–Palanpur and Ahmedabad–Samakhiali sections. The Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati Kavach project has been undertaken at a cost of ₹48 crore, according to the government. Work has also commenced on the doubling of the Sabarmati–Sarkhej railway line. HM Shah highlighted the capabilities of the WAG-12 locomotive, saying its 12,000-horsepower twin-section capacity enables it to haul freight equivalent to nearly 600 trucks. He said that while two locomotives were earlier required for such operations, a single WAG-12 can now undertake the task. Double-stack trains to boost freight capacity The Home Minister also highlighted the successful trial of the country’s first long-haul double-stack container train from Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai to Vadodara. He said India has a limited rail network available for freight movement and that successful deployment of double-stack freight trains could substantially increase freight-carrying capacity. HM Shah said an 11,000-km-long corridor is being converted into a four-lane network, which he said would facilitate movement towards the Delhi–Howrah and Delhi–Guwahati routes. He attributed the introduction of Dedicated Freight Corridors, Rapid Rail systems and upgraded railway stations to the modernisation of Indian Railways after Narendra Modi became Prime Minister in 2014. He also referred to the recent commissioning of a hydrogen-powered train, saying it placed India among the four countries possessing the technology. Diesel consumption falls as electrification expands HM Shah highlighted the reduction in railway diesel consumption, saying it declined from 293 crore litres in 2015–16 to 108 crore litres in 2024–25. He said railway electrification had expanded significantly, from about 30 per cent before 2014 to 99.6 per cent currently, with the remaining 0.4 per cent expected to be completed soon. articles.title: Amit Shah launches India's first LNG train, inaugurates Rs 1,472 crore projects
articles.content: ANI Photo | Amit Shah inaugurates Rs 1,472 crore worth development projects and launches India’s first LNG-powered train Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated development projects valued at Rs 1,472 crore and flagged off India’s first liquefied natural gas (LNG) powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, on September 28. Shah also opened the WAG-12 Maintenance Shed, established for maintaining railway locomotive engines, reportedly constructed at a cost of Rs 700 crore. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and other dignitaries were present at the event, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. Add TNM on Google During the programme, Shah outlined that multiple railway initiatives had commenced within the Sabarmati division, focusing on environmental sustainability, passenger amenities, and rail safety. He recalled that Sabarmati is historically significant as the starting point of experiments such as Satyagraha, simple living, rural development, and khadi. Shah noted the transformation of Sabarmati Railway Station from the 1980s, when passengers had to walk nearly two kilometres to find rickshaws, into a station with markedly improved connectivity, facilities, and safety. He emphasised that the projects inaugurated and foundation stones laid with a budget of Rs 1,472 crore would significantly benefit the region. ADVERTISEMENT He detailed that the WAG-12 Maintenance Shed supports maintenance for locomotives including the newly commissioned 12,000-horsepower twin-section WAG-12 engine, capable of hauling freight equivalent to 600 trucks alone, replacing the need for two locomotives previously required. Shah described this as a historic milestone for Indian Railways. In addition, the ‘Kavach’ train protection system has been installed on the Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati rail section at a cost of Rs 48 crore to enhance safety. Implementation of ‘Kavach’ is underway on Ahmedabad–Palanpur and Ahmedabad–Samakhiali rail sections, alongside the doubling of the Sabarmati–Sarkhej railway line. Shah highlighted the launch of the LNG-powered train as a major step toward environmental conservation. He recalled that since Narendra Modi assumed office as Prime Minister in 2014, the railways have seen the introduction of new facilities and modernisation of the network. ADVERTISEMENT He mentioned the successful trial of India’s first double-stack long-haul container train connecting Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust in Mumbai to Vadodara. Shah stated that the concept could nearly double freight-carrying capacity despite the limitation of existing tracks. He also referred to the ongoing conversion of an 11,000-kilometre corridor into a four-lane network to improve traffic flow towards Delhi–Howrah and Delhi–Guwahati. Shah attributed key projects such as Dedicated Freight Corridors, the Rapid Rail System, and premium railway stations to Prime Minister Modi’s leadership. He recalled the recent inauguration of a hydrogen-powered train by Modi, placing India among four countries possessing the technology. He stated that 97 per cent of bio-toilets and 87 per cent of LHB coaches are produced domestically under Modi’s government, with railway electrification increasing from 30 per cent to near completion during this period. articles.title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Station
articles.content: A hmedabad (Gujarat) [India], September 27 (ANI): Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the country's first LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas)-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Railway Station on Sunday, alongside launching several other Indian Railways projects in the Sabarmati Division. Advertisement Speaking on the occasion, Shah said the projects addressed environmental concerns, passenger convenience and safety. "Today marks the launch of various Indian Railways projects within the Sabarmati Division. These initiatives address environmental concerns, enhance passenger convenience, and bolster safety. In the past, I have frequently disembarked at Sabarmati Railway Station while travelling from Delhi. I extend my heartiest congratulations to the entire team, from the Sabarmati Railway Division to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, because seeing Sabarmati Station now, after so long, is remarkable," he said. Shah added that the station and its facilities had undergone a complete transformation with an investment of ₹1,472 crore. "A radical transformation has been achieved regarding passenger convenience, safety, and connectivity. The projects inaugurated and those for which foundation stones were laid today, involving an investment of ₹1,472 crore, will prove immensely beneficial for passengers in this region," he said. Highlighting the Railways' progress on reducing diesel dependency and expanding electrification, Shah said the railways' consumption of diesel has dropped from 293 crore litres to 108 crore. He stated, "In 2015-16, the railways consumed 293 crore litres of diesel. That figure has now dropped to 108 crore in 2024-25, and by 2030, we will bring it down to zero, thereby saving Indian currency. This is a massive achievement that often goes unnoticed." He further said, "Electrification covered just 75 kilometres in 2010-11, whereas in 2023-24, we electrified 7,188 kilometres in a single year. 99.6 per cent of the railway network is already electrified. We will complete the remaining 0.3 per cent as well. Only Sweden has achieved 100 per cent electrification globally, but there is a tenfold difference between the scale of Sweden's rail network and ours." Shah also took a swipe at the Congress over its track record on development. "The people of this country should question the Congress members, who spout all sorts of nonsense, about this vast disparity in development. In their last ten years, they did nothing but engage in scams, scandals, and corruption amounting to ₹12 lakh crore; yet, in 12 years, no one has been able to level even the slightest allegation of corruption against PM Modi," he said. Earlier in the day, Shah also attended a programme organised on the occasion of Acharya Shri Padmasagar Surishwar Ji Maharaj's 92nd birthday in Ahmedabad. (ANI)

articles.title: Home Minister flags off India's first LNG train, launches projects worth Rs 1,542 crore in Sabarmati
articles.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has launched India's first liquefied natural gas (LNG)-powered train from Sabarmati Station in Gujarat. The train uses a diesel-plus-LNG dual-fuel system developed for its Driving Power Cars (DPCs). The minister also launched projects worth over Rs 1,542 crore for railway safety, signalling, line capacity and freight infrastructure. He inaugurated the Rs 700-crore WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed at Sabarmati and flagged off a WAG-12 electric locomotive. Other projects involved the commissioning of the indigenous Kavach train protection system on the Ahmedabad-Palanpur and Ahmedabad-Samakhiyali sections, automatic signalling on two railway sections, and the launch of doubling work on the Sabarmati-Sarkhej section.
